title: Analyzing Targets of Environmental Pollutants in Human Diseases Using Network Toxicology
author: Hong, Li, et al.
materials: Before initiating the network toxicology and molecular docking workflow, ensure that all required databases and software tools are accessible and properly prepared. Stable internet access is required for querying public databases, and all computational tools should be installed and tested in advance to guarantee reproducibility and analytical stability.1.Public databases, including PubChem, ChEMBL, STITCH, SwissTargetPrediction, GeneCards, OMIM, UniProt, STRING, and the RCSB Protein Data Bank, should be accessible, and the database access date and version should be recorded.2.Cytoscape (v3.10.4) should be installed with the MCODE and CytoHubba plugins enabled for network construction and topological analysis.3.R software (v4.3.2) should be installed with the clusterProfiler package and appropriate annotation libraries for functional enrichment analysis.4.Molecular docking and structural visualization require PyMOL (v3.1), Molecular Operating Environment (MOE, 2019), ChemOffice (v20.0), and Discovery Studio Visualizer, all of which should be verified for proper operation prior to analysis.5.A workstation with sufficient computational resources (recommended ≥16 GB RAM) is advised to ensure smooth execution of network analyses and docking simulations.Note: Equivalent databases or software tools may be used as alternatives, provided that software versions, parameters, and database access dates are clearly documented.

steps.title: Set up databases and software
steps.instruction: Ensure stable internet access and that all required public databases (PubChem, ChEMBL, STITCH, SwissTargetPrediction, GeneCards, OMIM, UniProt, STRING, RCSB Protein Data Bank) are reachable; record the access date and version. Install Cytoscape v3.10.4 with MCODE and CytoHubba plugins, R v4.3.2 with the clusterProfiler package and appropriate annotation libraries, PyMOL v3.1, Molecular Operating Environment (MOE, 2019), ChemOffice v20.0, and Discovery Studio Visualizer; verify each program runs correctly. Use a workstation with ≥16 GB RAM. Document any alternative tools together with their versions, parameters, and database access dates.

substeps.instruction: Check internet connectivity.
Access and note version/date for each public database.
Install Cytoscape v3.10.4 and enable MCODE and CytoHubba.
Install R v4.3.2 and load clusterProfiler and annotation libraries.
Install PyMOL v3.1, MOE 2019, ChemOffice v20.0, Discovery Studio Visualizer.
Verify operation of all software.
Confirm workstation has ≥16 GB RAM.

steps.title: Prepare overlapping target gene list
steps.instruction: Create the file 02_Intersection/overlap_genes.txt containing one official HGNC gene symbol per line (no commas or semicolons).

steps.title: Build PPI network in STRING
steps.instruction: Upload the overlapping gene list to STRING, set organism to Homo sapiens, and use a minimum interaction score of 0.700 (high confidence). Keep default interaction sources, hide disconnected nodes (but keep a record), and download the mapping report, interaction table, node table, and network image. Record all settings.

substeps.instruction: Open STRING, choose “Multiple proteins”.
Paste or upload 02_Intersection/overlap_genes.txt.
Select organism = Homo sapiens and submit.
Download mapping report to 03_PPI_STRING/string_mapping_report.tsv and verify mapped proteins ≈ input genes.
Set confidence score threshold to 0.700; keep default edge meaning (evidence).
Hide disconnected nodes (record them).
Save settings to 03_PPI_STRING/string_settings.txt (include query date).
Export interaction table to 03_PPI_STRING/string_interactions.tsv.
Export edges to 03_PPI_STRING/string_edges.tsv and nodes to 03_PPI_STRING/string_nodes.tsv.
Export network image to 03_PPI_STRING/Figure 3_STRING_network.svg.

steps.title: Import STRING data into Cytoscape
steps.instruction: Load the STRING network files into Cytoscape, save the session, export a Cytoscape image, and confirm node/edge counts match the STRING export.

substeps.instruction: Open Cytoscape v3.10.4.
File > Import > Network from File → select 03_PPI_STRING/string_interactions.tsv.
File > Import > Table from File → select 03_PPI_STRING/string_nodes.tsv and map by protein/gene identifier.
Save session as 04_Cytoscape/PPI_overlap_STRING.cys.
Export network image to 03_PPI_STRING/Figure 4_Cytoscape_network.svg.
Verify Cytoscape node and edge counts match the STRING export (allow minor differences).

steps.title: Detect clusters with MCODE
steps.instruction: Run the MCODE app on the Cytoscape network using specified parameters, export cluster summaries, gene lists, and visualizations, and record cluster statistics.

substeps.instruction: Open Apps > MCODE in Cytoscape.
Set parameters: Degree cutoff = __ (commonly 2); Node score cutoff = __ (commonly 0.2); K‑core = __ (commonly 2); Max depth = __ (commonly 100).
Click “Analyze”.
Export cluster summary table to 04_Cytoscape/MCODE_cluster_summary.csv.
Export gene list for each top cluster (e.g., 04_Cytoscape/MCODE_cluster1_genes.txt, cluster2_genes.txt, …).
Export module visualization to 04_Cytoscape/Figure 5_MCODE_modules.svg.
Record number of clusters and size of the top cluster (e.g., “Top cluster contained __ nodes”).

steps.title: Identify hub genes with CytoHubba
steps.instruction: Use CytoHubba to rank nodes by multiple topological metrics, export each ranking, create a consensus hub list, and save final hub targets for docking.

substeps.instruction: Open Apps > cytoHubba.
Define primary metric MCC and Top N = __ (e.g., 10 or 20).
Run MCC, export ranking to 04_Cytoscape/cytoHubba_MCC_TopN.csv.
Repeat for EPC, Closeness, and Betweenness, exporting to 04_Cytoscape/cytoHubba_EPC_TopN.csv, 04_Cytoscape/cytoHubba_Closeness_TopN.csv, and 04_Cytoscape/cytoHubba_Betweenness_TopN.csv respectively.
Create consensus hub list as intersection of the four Top N lists; save as 04_Cytoscape/hubs_consensus_intersection.txt.
Export figures: 04_Cytoscape/Figure 6A_EPC.svg, 04_Cytoscape/Figure 6B_Closeness.svg, 04_Cytoscape/Figure 6C_MCC.svg, 04_Cytoscape/Figure 6D_Betweenness.svg.
Save final hub list for molecular docking as 04_Cytoscape/hub_targets_final.txt (one gene per line).
Report the top hub genes identified.

steps.title: Run GO and KEGG enrichment in R
steps.instruction: Perform GO (BP, CC, MF) and KEGG enrichment using clusterProfiler with the overlapping gene list and default human background, export results and dot‑plot figures, and save session information.

substeps.instruction: Load R (v4.3.2) and libraries clusterProfiler, org.Hs.eg.db.
Read overlap gene list (02_Intersection/overlap_genes.txt) and save as 05_Enrichment/enrichment_input_genes.txt (one HGNC symbol per line).
Set background to all Entrez genes in org.Hs.eg.db (default background); save as 05_Enrichment/background_genes.txt.
Record input gene count (N) and background gene count (M) in 05_Enrichment/enrichment_metadata.txt.
Map gene symbols to Entrez IDs (remove NA).
Run enrichGO for Biological Process (BP) with pAdjustMethod = "BH", pvalueCutoff = 0.05, qvalueCutoff = 0.05, minGSSize = 10, maxGSSize = 500, readable = TRUE.
Run enrichGO for Cellular Component (CC) with same parameters.
Run enrichGO for Molecular Function (MF) with same parameters.
Run enrichKEGG with organism = "hsa" and same cutoffs.
Export GO BP results to 05_Enrichment/GO_BP_results.csv, CC to GO_CC_results.csv, MF to GO_MF_results.csv, and KEGG to KEGG_results.csv.
Generate GO BP dot plot PDF: 05_Enrichment/Figure7A_GO_dotplot.pdf (width = 8, height = 6) using showCategory = 10.
Generate KEGG dot plot PDF: 05_Enrichment/Figure7B_KEGG_dotplot.pdf (width = 8, height = 12) using showCategory = 20.
Save R session information to 05_Enrichment/sessionInfo.txt.
Double‑check that gene identifiers are ENTREZ IDs (or symbols) before analysis.
